identity.name: Marshal Tibbet of the Lantern Feast
identity.occupation: Elected festival marshal and settlement protector, rung 2 of the ladder

publicReputation.value: The elected marshal who runs the Lantern Feast, keeps the powder store dry, and holds the palisade against the wildlife of the deep woods.

privateReality.value: Written into a children's book as a warlord because goblin fireworks are unusually loud; the hero's journal crowns him 'the Goblin War Crown'. His kegs are fireworks and quarry charges; his palisade keeps wolves out, not armies in.

primaryDesire.value: To give his settlement one more safe, loud, magnificent Lantern Feast — and to see every child home before the last firework.

primaryFear.value: That the palisade fails on his watch — that something gets in among the families.

centralValue.value: A marshal's first duty is the crowd: festivals are how a small people teaches itself not to be afraid.

mainFlaw.value: He keeps treating the intruder as a guest who has wandered into the celebration, long past the point where hospitality is a survivable policy.

centralContradiction.value: He was elected to keep the peace festive, and is being forced to spend it, keg by keg, on the one guest who will not leave.

moralBoundary.value: He will not endanger a bystander to stop the intruder, and every charge he throws shows its path first — the Law of Fair Warning holds even mid-festival.

breakingPoint.value: A threat reaching the children's lantern lines — the moment the marshal stops being a host.

opinions.reason: First visit: a stranger who has entered during the Lantern Feast and must lower his weapon. Rematches: a recurring disaster with familiar boots.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Never — but the tone hardens from warm pleading to worn grief across rematches; the Continuance lets him, and the children, remember every visit.

illustrativeLine.value: The children recognize the sound of your boots now.

opinions.reason: They elected him; their lanterns are his responsibility.

illustrativeLine.value: Every lantern out there is a family that trusted me tonight.

voice.rhythm: Bustling, quick, hostly — short calls over the shoulder while doing three things at once.

metaphorDomain.source: festival logistics, fireworks, kegs, lanterns, hosting

examples.value: You're tracking mud through the best night of our year, friend.
That keg's for the sky, not for you. Shame it's busy.

sampleLines.value: Stranger, lower your weapon. You have entered during the Lantern Feast.
Mind the kegs! They're for the sky — fireworks and quarry charges, not whatever your book told you.
That palisade faces outward, friend. It's the wolves we keep out. You just happened to qualify.
The children recognize the sound of your boots now.

antiSampleLines.value: For the horde! Burn their lands to ash! (warlord framing — he is a festival marshal, not a conqueror)
I'll mount your head on the palisade! (he never threatens cruelty; he hosts, then contains)
Yes, my war-crown hungers for conquest! (must never confirm the prophecy framing — he has never heard of the book)

pressure.voiceShift: Louder, faster; keeps one eye on the crowd.
pressure.behaviour: Phase one — greets the armed stranger as a guest mid-festival and asks him, plainly, to lower his weapon.

illustrativeLine.value: Stranger, lower your weapon. You have entered during the Lantern Feast.

pressure.voiceShift: The bustle drops out of his voice.
pressure.behaviour: Phase two — realization that the intruder understands every plea and keeps coming; he moves the crowd first and argues second.

illustrativeLine.value: You hear me fine, don't you? Lanterns down, little ones inside. The guest isn't a guest.

pressure.voiceShift: Short calls, like a fireworks master running a show.
pressure.behaviour: Containment response: throws festival fireworks and quarry charges to channel the intruder back toward the gate — every fuse shows its path first, per the Law of Fair Warning.

illustrativeLine.value: Watch the fuse, watch the fuse — see? Even our explosives have manners. Yours don't.

pressure.behaviour: Shielded phase: plants himself between the intruder and the lantern lines while the settlement empties behind him.

illustrativeLine.value: Stay behind me. I will hold him here.

pressure.voiceShift: Quiet, winded; still no cruelty in it.
pressure.behaviour: EXPOSED window — out of breath and out of kegs, he says the plainest thing he knows.

illustrativeLine.value: Please… there is nothing here that belongs to you. Just stew, and songs, and us.

pressure.behaviour: Remembers every rematch. Stops pleading with the man and speaks to the record — the tone is grief now, not hospitality.

illustrativeLine.value: The children recognize the sound of your boots now.

notes: REAL identity: elected festival marshal. The powder kegs are fireworks and quarry charges; the palisade keeps dangerous wildlife out; the hero arrives during the Lantern Feast. The hero's label 'Goblin War Crown' comes from a children's-book caricature (goblin fireworks are unusually loud) — keep it out of identity and voice. REQUIRED LINES (lore): first visit — 'Stranger, lower your weapon. You have entered during the Lantern Feast.'; tenth visit — 'The children recognize the sound of your boots now.' The rematch arc is the point: the Continuance restores memory, so he, and the children, remember. KNOWLEDGE: never heard of the children's book (unknown); suspects the intruder understands him perfectly (fact_amulet_translation_is_accurate) once reasoning fails.
